purpose: Seventeenth expanded public source layer focused on route-choice boundaries that are not ordinary templates: stereochemical model transfer and chiral catalyst scope, protecting-group orthogonality and deprotection sequencing, salt resolution and chiral crystallization, solid-phase synthesis impurity lineage, late-stage diversification and SAR source lineage, hazardous-reagent substitution and process safety, feedstock and supply-chain route risk, and analytical identity/reference-standard/stability policy.

promotion_requirements: manual chemist, process, analytical, safety, regulatory, supply-chain, and medicinal-chemistry review

explicit stereochemical model, protecting-group sequence, resolution/crystallization evidence, solid-phase impurity lineage, SAR comparator series, hazard-substitution rationale, supply-chain provenance, or analytical identity/stability evidence before proposal promotion
separate stereochemical, protecting-group, chiral-resolution, solid-phase, SAR-library, hazardous-reagent, feedstock, and analytical-reference policy

route-specific substrate scope, matched/mismatched model evidence, deprotection compatibility, mother-liquor or impurity fate, deletion-sequence/capping evidence, biological-mode or assay lineage, thermal/reactive hazard evidence, supplier/quality traceability, and stability-indicating analytical method review
safety, toxicology, chiral-purity, bioactive-series, process-hazard, regulatory, supply-chain, analytical-validation, and storage-stability review where relevant
safety_scope: records intentionally avoid quantities, operating conditions, hazardous execution instructions, purification recipes, and scale-up protocols

v18 records are route-choice and source-quality priors only and must not auto-close routes as stock, validated resolution processes, safe substitutions, supply-secure feedstocks, or stability-qualified reference standards

families.name: Stereochemical model transfer, matched/mismatched chiral control, and chiral catalyst or auxiliary scope
families.strategic_principle: Separate a formal asymmetric disconnection from the stereochemical model that makes it trustworthy. Catalyst, auxiliary, enzyme, or substrate-control records need matched/mismatched evidence and analogue scope before they can guide route ranking.

families.name: Protecting-group orthogonality, lability, and deprotection-sequence policy
families.strategic_principle: Separate a protected precursor from the sequence logic that installs and removes protection. Route value depends on orthogonality, lability, late-stage compatibility, waste, and deprotection endpoint evidence.

families.name: Diastereomeric salt resolution, crystallization, conglomerate behavior, and chiral-purity boundaries
families.strategic_principle: Separate racemate access from resolution evidence. A salt, cocrystal, or conglomerate route must carry crystallization behavior, yield/purity tradeoff, mother-liquor fate, and chiral analytical support.

families.name: Solid-phase peptide, oligonucleotide, capping, deletion-sequence, cleavage, and impurity-lineage policy
families.strategic_principle: Separate solid-phase route convenience from cycle efficiency and impurity lineage. Deletion sequences, insertions, depurination, capping, cleavage, and purification difficulty are strategic source fields.

families.name: Late-stage diversification, SAR-library source lineage, comparator series, and assay provenance
families.strategic_principle: Separate a diversification handle from evidence that the analogue series is meaningful. SAR-library records need parent series, comparator compounds, site-selectivity, assay lineage, and biological-mode context.

families.name: Hazardous-reagent substitution, reactive intermediate containment, and process-safety route policy
families.strategic_principle: Separate chemical feasibility from scalable safety. Strategic value can come from replacing or containing hazardous reagents, but promotion requires hazard evaluation, compatibility, and process-safety evidence.

families.name: Feedstock availability, supplier traceability, raw-material quality, and supply-chain route-risk boundary
families.strategic_principle: Separate a purchasable-looking precursor from a resilient route anchor. Feedstock records need source, quality, supplier, geopolitical/logistic risk, regulatory grade, and change-control provenance.

families.name: Analytical identity, reference standard, degradant/metabolite, tautomer/salt, and stability-policy boundaries
families.strategic_principle: Separate target or impurity name from analytical identity and stability evidence. Reference-standard, degradant, metabolite, salt, tautomer, and storage records need validated methods and stability-indicating provenance.

anchors.name: Stereochemical-control anchor with reviewed catalyst/auxiliary/substrate model, matched/mismatched cases, and analogue scope
Protecting-group sequence anchor with reviewed orthogonality, lability, deprotection order, and endpoint compatibility
Resolution/crystallization anchor with reviewed salt/cocrystal behavior, mother-liquor fate, yield/purity tradeoff, and chiral assay
Solid-phase synthesis anchor with reviewed cycle efficiency, capping, deletion/insertion sequences, cleavage, and impurity lineage
Late-stage diversification/SAR anchor with reviewed parent series, site selectivity, analogue comparator, assay lineage, and biological mode
Process-safety anchor with reviewed hazardous reagent or intermediate, safer alternative, containment mode, and scale boundary
Feedstock/supply-chain anchor with reviewed supplier, quality grade, source traceability, logistics, and change-control risk
Analytical identity/stability anchor with reviewed reference standard, degradant/metabolite identity, validated method, and storage evidence

disconnections.name: Stereodefined product to chiral catalyst/substrate model plus matched/mismatched scope policy

forward_logic: separate the bond-forming transformation from the stereochemical model that predicts product configuration
track catalyst identity, substrate class, matched/mismatched cases, and product stereochemical assignment
avoid transferring enantioselectivity claims outside the reviewed analogue scope
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Reward asymmetric route sources only when stereochemical model, substrate scope, and matched/mismatched evidence are explicit.

evidence.citation: Asymmetric catalysis in complex target synthesis discusses catalyst/substrate control and the need for predictable stereochemical performance.
Stereochemical cooperativity review discusses matched pairings and ligand chirality elements in asymmetric catalyst optimization.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit catalyst/substrate model, matched and mismatched examples, analogue scope, and configuration proof

disconnections.name: Auxiliary-controlled stereocenter to auxiliary installation, cleavage/recovery, and transferability policy

break_bonds: product stereocenter to auxiliary-controlled precursor boundary
forward_logic: separate stereoselective formation from auxiliary installation and removal
track auxiliary recovery, cleavage compatibility, stereochemical assignment, and mass-balance burden
penalize routes where auxiliary use hides extra steps or problematic deprotection
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Use auxiliary records when stereochemical reliability must be weighed against installation/removal burden.

evidence.citation: SuperQuat chiral auxiliary review discusses design, synthetic uses, cleavage, and recovery considerations.
Transition-state model review discusses how chiral information is transferred in asymmetric catalysis.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit auxiliary installation, stereochemical model, cleavage compatibility, and recovery or waste policy

disconnections.name: Functionalized target to orthogonally protected precursor plus protection/deprotection order policy

forward_logic: separate functional-group masking from the strategic order in which groups are revealed
track orthogonal removal, lability, downstream compatibility, and endpoint identity
flag routes where a protecting group solves one step but blocks a later strategic move
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Reward protecting-group routes only when protection role and deprotection order are explicit.

risks: extra steps hidden in route score

evidence.citation: Orthogonality review traces orthogonal protecting-group strategy from solid-phase synthesis into broader chemistry.
Oligosaccharide protecting-group review discusses challenges in late-stage functionalization and global deprotection.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit protection role, orthogonality, deprotection order, endpoint identity, and downstream compatibility

disconnections.name: Globally protected route to final target plus lability, waste, and protecting-group-free comparator policy

break_bonds: final target to globally protected precursor boundary
forward_logic: separate formal convergence from the late unmasking operation that determines whether the route survives
track protecting-group count, deprotection endpoint, waste/step burden, and sensitive functionality
prefer routes with explicit deprotection evidence or credible protecting-group-free comparators
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Down-rank protection-heavy routes when final deprotection lacks endpoint evidence or damages key functionality.

evidence.citation: Protecting-group-free synthesis review frames protection/deprotection as step and waste burden in complex molecule synthesis.
Carbohydrate-building-block review covers protection/deprotection strategy for selectively protected intermediates.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit final deprotection evidence, lability assessment, protecting-group count, and comparator route

disconnections.name: Enantiopure product to racemate plus diastereomeric salt/cocrystal resolution and mother-liquor policy

forward_logic: separate racemate synthesis from the resolution operation that controls enantiomeric purity
track resolving agent, salt or cocrystal behavior, mother-liquor recycling, assay method, and yield/purity tradeoff
avoid treating resolution as a generic purification without mass-balance and chiral analytical evidence
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Reward salt-resolution routes only when crystal behavior, mother-liquor fate, and chiral assay are explicit.

evidence.citation: Chiral separation review surveys resolution strategies from racemate to enantiomer including salt and cocrystal approaches.
Chiral-drugs overview discusses classical chiral resolution by diastereomer formation and crystallization.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit resolving agent, salt/cocrystal behavior, assay, yield/purity tradeoff, and recycle policy

disconnections.name: Chiral product to conglomerate or preferential crystallization plus seeding and purity-policy boundary

forward_logic: separate a molecular stereocenter from the solid-form behavior that enables resolution
track conglomerate evidence, seeding mode, phase behavior, and bulk chiral purity assay
flag routes where single-crystal information is overinterpreted as bulk enantiopurity
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Use crystallization-policy records when solid-form behavior, not a new bond, is the strategic source.

evidence.citation: Crystallization-based deracemization review covers chiral resolution of small molecules.
Hidden conglomerate chiral-pool study discusses manual review of synthetic and crystallographic route evidence.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit conglomerate evidence, phase behavior, seed lineage, and bulk chiral-purity assay

disconnections.name: Peptide target to SPPS cycle plan plus deletion/insertion, capping, cleavage, and purification policy

forward_logic: separate peptide sequence assembly from the impurity lineage produced by each solid-phase cycle
track deletion and insertion sequences, capping policy, difficult sequence features, cleavage endpoint, and purification assay
avoid treating SPPS as automatically feasible for long or impurity-prone sequences
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Reward SPPS routes only when cycle failure modes and impurity fate are represented.

evidence.citation: Peptide impurity review identifies SPPS-related deletion and insertion impurities among peptide medicines.
Fluorous capping reagent paper frames capping as a way to control deletion products in SPPS purification.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit sequence, cycle efficiency, capping, deletion/insertion profile, cleavage endpoint, and purification assay

disconnections.name: Oligonucleotide product to solid-phase cycle plus deletion, depurination, capping, and degradant policy

forward_logic: separate target sequence from solid-phase synthesis error accumulation
track deletion frequency, capping chemistry class, depurination/degradant risk, and sequence-verification method
flag sequences where impurity similarity makes purification or analytical assignment route-defining
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Use oligonucleotide solid-phase records when deletion or degradant lineage dominates route trust.

evidence.citation: Oligonucleotide impurity review discusses synthesis-cycle impurities and degradants characterized by mass spectrometry.
Capping-step study examines how solid-phase phosphoramidite capping conditions affect oligonucleotide synthetic errors.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit cycle error model, deletion/degradant profile, capping policy, sequence assay, and purification strategy

disconnections.name: Lead analogue to parent scaffold plus late-stage diversification and SAR comparator-series policy

forward_logic: separate a late-stage functionalization handle from evidence that the analogue series is meaningful
track parent scaffold, site selectivity, comparator analogues, assay lineage, and biological-mode context
avoid promoting a single analogue as strategic source without series-level evidence
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Reward late-stage diversification records when they expose parent-series and assay lineage, not just a modified product.

evidence.citation: Medicinal-chemistry LSF review frames late-stage functionalization as a strategy for SAR exploration.
Natural-product diversification review discusses late-stage transformations for drug discovery and chemical biology.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit parent scaffold, site selectivity, comparator series, assay lineage, and biological-mode context

disconnections.name: Library hit to encoded-library synthesis lineage plus resynthesis, assay, and validation policy

forward_logic: separate encoded-library selection signal from independently validated chemical matter
track library synthesis route, DNA-compatible transformation, enrichment context, resynthesis, and orthogonal assay
down-rank hits without source lineage or validation outside the encoded context
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Use encoded-library records as weak route sources unless resynthesis and assay validation are explicit.

evidence.citation: DNA-encoded library review summarizes DEL construction, screening, successes, and future challenges.
DEL late-stage functionalization review discusses DNA-compatible diversification and limitations.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit library synthesis lineage, enrichment context, resynthesis, orthogonal assay, and comparator series

disconnections.name: Target route to hazardous reagent or intermediate plus safer substitution and process-safety boundary

forward_logic: separate chemical yield from hazard burden and scale transfer
track hazardous reagent class, substitution rationale, waste/toxicity tradeoff, and process-safety evidence
avoid promoting a safer-sounding route without hazard and exposure review
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Reward hazard substitutions only when hazard identity, compatibility, and process-safety evidence are explicit.

risks: hazard shifted to workup or waste

evidence.citation: Process-safety review discusses thermal and reaction hazard evaluation in pharmaceutical process development.
Green-toxicology article discusses avoiding regrettable substitutions during safer chemical design.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit hazard identity, safer alternative rationale, compatibility, waste/exposure review, and scale boundary

disconnections.name: Reactive intermediate route to continuous-flow containment plus heat/mass-transfer and safety-policy boundary

forward_logic: separate generation of a hazardous intermediate from containment and consumption strategy
track flow rationale, residence/hold-up concept, heat/mass-transfer advantage, inline monitoring, and downstream compatibility
flag routes where flow is claimed as safety evidence without process review
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Use flow-containment records when process format is the strategic source of feasibility.

evidence.citation: Diazo/diazonium flow review discusses continuous processing as a way to handle hazardous reactive species.
Flow-chemistry API review discusses safety, heat/mass-transfer, and process-control advantages for pharmaceutical synthesis.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit reactive intermediate, containment rationale, inline monitoring, downstream compatibility, and scale boundary

disconnections.name: Route anchor to feedstock availability, quality grade, supplier diversity, and change-control policy

forward_logic: separate market availability from route resilience
track supplier count, source geography, quality grade, impurity profile, and change-control requirements
avoid auto-closing routes on feedstocks whose availability or quality provenance is weak
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Reward feedstock anchors only when supplier, quality, and change-control evidence are explicit.

evidence.citation: Systematic review of pharmaceutical supply-chain risks identifies supply and supplier issues as major risk categories.
ICH Q10 pharmaceutical quality-system guidance includes material acquisition and control concepts.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit supplier/source, quality grade, impurity profile, logistics, and change-control evidence

disconnections.name: API route precursor to raw-material procurement, traceability, and supplier-control boundary

forward_logic: separate a named raw material from evidence that its source and quality are controlled
track procurement pathway, manufacturer, traceability, grade, testing, and supplier-change impact
flag routes where outsourcing or raw-material opacity changes strategic feasibility
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Use raw-material traceability records when supplier control is route-defining.

evidence.citation: API procurement/manufacture qualitative study highlights raw-material and API supply-chain steps that are often overlooked.
Traceability review discusses technologies and critical factors for safer pharmaceutical supply chains.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit supplier qualification, source traceability, raw-material tests, grade, and supplier-change policy

disconnections.name: Impurity, degradant, or metabolite target to reference-standard identity plus validated analytical method policy

forward_logic: separate a proposed impurity or metabolite structure from analytical proof of identity
track reference standard provenance, purity, structural assignment, validated method, and intended assay use
avoid treating an unqualified synthetic byproduct as an analytical standard
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Reward reference-standard routes only when identity, purity, and method validation evidence are explicit.

evidence.citation: ICH Q2(R2) provides guidance for validation of analytical procedures.
Critical impurity review discusses analytical detection of impurities and degradation products in APIs and drug products.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit identity assignment, purity, reference provenance, validated method, and intended assay use

disconnections.name: Analytical target to stability-indicating method plus storage, salt/tautomer, and degradation policy

forward_logic: separate successful synthesis from evidence that the analytical target remains the assigned identity over time
track stability-indicating method, storage state, salt/tautomer assignment, degradation pathways, and retest policy
flag reference routes where storage or identity drift undermines source reliability
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Use stability-policy records when target identity or source trust depends on storage and degradation evidence.

evidence.citation: ICH Q1A(R2) defines stability data expectations for new drug substances and products.
Guidelines and pharmacopoeial standards review discusses pharmaceutical impurity standards and risk assessment.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit stability-indicating method, storage state, salt/tautomer identity, degradant profile, and retest policy

source_notes.summary: The v18 expansion promotes backlog families covering stereochemical source transfer, protecting-group sequence policy, chiral resolution, solid-phase impurity lineage, SAR-library lineage, hazard substitution, supply-chain risk, and analytical identity/stability.

V18 records are advisory. Promotion requires route-specific model, sequence, impurity, assay, process-safety, supply-chain, or analytical evidence; hazardous-reagent, resolution, solid-phase, library, and regulatory records must not be treated as validated procedures by default.
